beats.title: The mismatch
beats.text: This model predicts one hundred thousand dollars for a house labeled two hundred thousand. How can that mistake teach it?

beats.title: Make a prediction
beats.text: We measure size in thousands of square feet, and price in hundred-thousands. The model predicts weight times size. Here, both start at one, so it predicts one hundred thousand dollars.

beats.title: Measure the error
beats.text: The label is two. Prediction minus label is negative one. Half the squared error gives a loss of point five.

beats.title: Follow the slope
beats.text: The loss slope against the weight is error times size: negative one. Increasing the weight will lower the loss. With a step size of point five, gradient descent moves the weight from one to one point five.

beats.title: Check the result
beats.text: Now the prediction is one hundred fifty thousand dollars, and the loss falls to point one two five. This update reduced the error on this example.

beats.title: The learning loop
beats.text: Training repeats this process across examples: predict, measure error, adjust, repeat. Real models are more complex, and one example is not enough to guarantee good predictions on new houses.
